digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### SpaceX may spend up to $119B on 'Terafab' chip factory in Texas
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/spacex-may-spend-up-to-119-billion-on-terafab-chip-factory-in-texas/
Musk moves to vertically integrate semiconductor supply for Starlink and xAI.
A $119B commitment would dwarf TSMC's Arizona fab ($40B) and Intel's Ohio project ($20B). This signals SpaceX sees chip access as existential—likely driven by compute demands from xAI's Colossus cluster and Starlink's growing satellite constellation. Watch for CHIPS Act subsidy applications.

### SQLite Is a Library of Congress Recommended Storage Format
URL: https://sqlite.org/locrsf.html
Federal archivists now endorse SQLite for long-term data preservation.
This institutional validation cements SQLite's position as critical infrastructure, not just a lightweight database. For PE: companies building on SQLite (Turso, Cloudflare D1) now have a regulatory tailwind. The format's 700+ trillion active databases make this the most deployed software architecture decision ever ratified by a preservation authority.

### Genesis AI has gone full stack, demo shows
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/khosla-backed-robotics-startup-genesis-ai-has-gone-full-stack-demo-shows/
Khosla's $105M seed bet reveals GENE-26.5 model plus dexterous manipulation hardware.
The "full stack" approach—owning both foundation model and physical robot—mirrors the playbook that worked for Tesla FSD. Most robotics startups pick one; Genesis chose both. Complex manipulation demos suggest they're targeting manufacturing and logistics verticals where unit economics justify premium pricing.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### DeepSeek could hit $45B valuation from its first investment round
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/deepseek-could-hit-45b-valuation-from-its-first-investment-round/
Chinese AI lab that embarrassed OpenAI on efficiency now commands near-parity valuation.
At $45B, DeepSeek would match Anthropic's last round despite training models at 10-20x lower compute cost. This reprices the entire AI capex thesis—if frontier models don't require $10B clusters, the hyperscaler GPU hoarding strategy looks increasingly like a bubble. U.S. AI labs face margin compression.

### Insurance startup Corgi hits $1.3B valuation 4 months after its Series A
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/insurance-startup-corgi-hits-1-3b-valuation-4-months-after-its-series-a/
TCV leads $160M round at 6x+ step-up in four months.
Insurtech was left for dead after Lemonade and Root collapsed. Corgi's velocity suggests either genuine product-market fit or a flight to "real revenue" verticals as AI hype cools. TCV's involvement (Spotify, Netflix track record) adds credibility. Worth tracking their loss ratios versus legacy carriers.

### Snap says its $400M deal with Perplexity 'amicably ended'
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/snap-says-its-400m-deal-with-perplexity-amicably-ended/
High-profile AI integration deal unwinds before launch.
The collapse of a $400M partnership suggests either Perplexity's unit economics don't survive at consumer scale, or Snap balked at the engagement metrics. Either way, this cools expectations for AI search as a licensable product. Perplexity's path to profitability just got murkier.

### Robinhood's venture fund IPO attracted 150,000+ retail investors
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/robinhoods-venture-fund-ipo-attracted-150000-retail-investors-ceo-says/
Retail gets pre-IPO exposure to OpenAI, Stripe, Databricks via Robinhood wrapper.
This is financial engineering, not venture capital—Robinhood is essentially securitizing secondary market access. With 150K participants at likely $500-5K tickets, they've created $75M-750M in AUM with zero GP commitment. Watch for regulatory scrutiny on liquidity terms and valuation disclosure.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Vibe coding and agentic engineering are getting closer than I'd like
URL: https://simonwillison.net/2026/May/6/vibe-coding-and-agentic-engineering/
Simon Willison sounds the alarm on AI agents writing code with minimal human oversight.
Willison—one of the most credible voices on practical AI tooling—is flagging that current "agentic" coding workflows lack the verification loops that make them safe. Translation: enterprises adopting AI dev tools without guardrails are accumulating technical debt they can't see yet. Long-term bullish for code verification and testing infrastructure.

### From Supabase to Clerk to Better Auth
URL: https://blog.val.town/better-auth
Val.town documents migration path through three auth providers in production.
This is a real-world postmortem on developer infrastructure switching costs. Val.town's journey reveals that auth—supposedly a solved problem—still has enough friction to justify multiple rewrites. For special situations: auth startups (Clerk, WorkOS, Stytch) may face higher churn than investor models assume. Lock-in is weaker than it looks.

### Microsoft's AI data center push is colliding with its clean power goals
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/microsofts-ai-data-center-push-is-colliding-with-its-clean-power-goals/
Azure's AI expansion threatens Microsoft's 2030 carbon-negative commitment.
Microsoft is now facing the math: each new AI data center requires 300-500MW of power, and renewable capacity isn't scaling fast enough. This creates regulatory risk in ESG-conscious jurisdictions and opens the door for nuclear-forward competitors. The company that partnered with Helion may need to accelerate that timeline dramatically.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The week's signal: infrastructure trumps model innovation. SpaceX building chips, DeepSeek proving efficiency beats scale, Microsoft hitting power walls—the AI race is shifting from "who has the best model" to "who controls compute, power, and silicon." The Perplexity-Snap collapse suggests the consumer AI search market may be smaller than assumed, while Corgi's insurtech velocity hints that capital is rotating toward vertical AI with measurable unit economics. The real alpha is in the picks-and-shovels layer where physical constraints dominate.
